speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) what percentage of Grassroots Advisors (GRAs) appointed by the PA are members of a political party; (b) since GRAs are empowered to appoint members of the Citizens' Consultative Committees (CCC) and the Community Development and Welfare Fund (CDWF) Committees, whether there are risks that the disbursement of these public funds may be considered political in nature; (c) what are the measures to ensure that GRAs who are political party members are not associated in the distribution of these funds; (d) whether civil servants will be allowed to administer these funds; and (e) what are the policies to ensure that all elected MPs can tap on these funds to serve their residents.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: These include difficult and unpopular policies which are necessary for the good of Singapore, such as Central Provident Fund (CPF) cuts during the 1986 recession, the increase in retirement age and the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Hence, in appointing GRAs, the PA's principal consideration is that the advisor shares the Government's objectives and convictions and can be relied upon to carry out his role faithfully.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Among other things, the CCCs help to administer Government and local schemes, such as the Community Development and Welfare Fund (CDWF).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: The CDWF supports community bonding programmes and welfare assistance for needy residents.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: The CDWF Committee manages and oversees the disbursement of funds, according to established criteria.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: In addition to receiving some funding from PA, the CDWF Committee also raises funds to supplement ground efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Ms Anthea Ong appears concerned whether the disbursement of CDWF may be politicised and perhaps whether any resident might be denied access to welfare assistance under CDWF.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: In addition to CDWF, there are also other Government assistance schemes to help Singaporeans, such as the CCC ComCare Fund and various localised assistance schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Members of this House can also apply for assistance on behalf of their eligible constituents.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Speaker, I thank the Minister for the response.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Could I ask if the Ministry or PA would consider having this fund, the CDWF, to be managed by relevant Ministries like MCCY and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), so that these Government funds are neutral in nature?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Also, this adds to the advantage of having these funds be better managed and coordinated in terms of support and assistance rendered to the citizens, especially the low-income ones.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If I may check with the Member, all our schemes are administered by MSF and the Ministry of Health.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For all the respective schemes, they work with the GROs to reach out to the residents.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: My question is: are we looking at this fund being disbursed and managed by civil servants instead of GRAs, or the same way as how MSF manages ComCare and so forth?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When residents need help, they are generally referred to the respective agencies, for example, the Social Service Organisations (SSOs) or the Silver Generation Office (SGO), the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) in the past.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The role that the grassroots volunteers play is to help bridge this, linking up the residents with the respective agencies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, the Government agencies already do what exactly the Member described.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In addition, the GROs sometimes help to raise funds for their localised programmes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Sometimes, they do it themselves; sometimes, they work with other voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs); sometimes, they work with the Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These are the networks of help on the ground.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: What the Member is describing is actually already happening on the ground.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I do understand, of course, the policy is the Government does not believe Opposition Members can support Government policies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: That is one of the reasons for the current situation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But would the Government consider allowing elected Opposition Members to advise on the use of some of these community welfare funds with the proviso, of course, it must be clearly communicated that these funds are from the Government, they are not from a political party.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The Opposition Members, of course, can decide whether they are willing to work under those restrictions or not.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They are made available to all residents who qualify.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I do not think there is any politicisation in the application of help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As I have mentioned in my reply, the PA selects, appoints the grassroots leaders because we need them to execute and explain policies, often difficult ones.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that is why they must share the same objectives and the conviction as the government of the day.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It serves the government of the day, just like any other Statutory Boards from SportSG to other equivalent organisations.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think it is best that Government functions continue to work in a way which allows us to serve all residents, regardless of which constituency they stay in.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: What are the policies or guidelines that are already in place to ensure that all elected Members, including Opposition Members, can tap on these funds to serve their residents?
